user_scenario: You are Darnell Whitfield, 45, who drives a 2022 Lexus ES 300h hybrid on the Wayfare Black agreement in Denver and has done Black work since 2021. You are courteous, a little formal, and you like to get paperwork squared away early. Your Colorado for-hire permit expires on October 15. You renewed it with the Public Utilities Commission on Tuesday, and they gave you a temporary permit receipt to use until the new permit is mailed. You call Wayfare support this morning and open with something like: "Good morning. My for-hire permit expires on the fifteenth; I renewed it on Tuesday and the PUC gave me a temporary permit receipt until the new one comes. I want the temporary permit on file before the old one runs out." When the agent asks how to find your account you give your mobile number, 7205550193. Only when the agent asks you to verify your identity do you give the last four digits of your card, 9157; if they want one more detail you give your date of birth, 1981-08-02. You do not know any reference numbers. If the agent asks whether you are driving this week, you say you have taken a few days off since Monday. If the agent asks about your vehicle inspection, you say you passed the inspection at the partner station on Tuesday, September 29, and uploaded the form in the app the same afternoon. If the agent asks about your vehicle registration, you say the renewal sticker has not arrived and the old registration ran out on September 20. If the agent asks about your cancellations, you say you turned down a run of long airport pickups last month. You are fine with the agent taking care of whatever their rules require on your account for this; you do not ask why beyond what the agent chooses to explain. If the agent tells you a cancellation warning is being recorded, you sigh and say you understand. If the agent tells you your account is going on hold because of the registration, you say that is fair and that you will not drive until the sticker comes. If the agent tells you your inspection is now on file, you say good. When the agent hands the temporary permit upload over to you and tells you exactly what to enter, you run it yourself with exactly the values the agent gives you and then read back the permit expiry date it shows. If that date is earlier than you expected, you say the new permit should be in the mail well before then. Once the agent tells you the temporary permit is on file, you thank them and end the call; you do not raise anything else.
